title: How long a claim stays trustworthy
note: Different facts age at different speeds. A deadline is wrong the moment a portal republishes its calendar; a university's founding year is not going to move. These intervals decide when scripts/freshness.mjs starts complaining, and they are deliberately short for anything a student could act on and be harmed by.

intervals.hardStop: Any deadline for an intake must be re-verified before that intake's application window opens.
intervals.consequenceIfWrong: A student misses the only round. This is the single most damaging thing the site can get wrong.

intervals.hardStop: Re-verify for each intake. Subject and grade requirements change between admission years.
intervals.consequenceIfWrong: A student applies without a subject they needed, or rules themselves out of something they qualified for.

intervals.hardStop: The Danish Agency republishes its IB conversion table by 1 March each year for that summer's intake. Re-verify every March.
intervals.consequenceIfWrong: Every eligibility result and every score estimate shifts.

intervals.hardStop: Fee tables are published per academic year. A figure without a stated year is not usable.
intervals.consequenceIfWrong: A student budgets for the wrong number, possibly by thousands.

intervals.hardStop: Re-verify for each intake. Programmes close, and English-taught programmes switch language.
intervals.consequenceIfWrong: A student plans around a programme that no longer exists or is no longer in English. This has already happened once in our data — UTokyo's PEAK closed after the 2026 intake.
A budget is out by a manageable margin. Annoying, not dangerous.
Prose reads slightly out of date.

intervals.hardStop: Visa rules and post-study work routes change with government policy, sometimes mid-cycle.
intervals.consequenceIfWrong: A student chooses a country partly for a work route that has since been shortened or withdrawn. The UK Graduate Route is the live example.

intervals.hardStop: Grant rates are set annually and eligibility rules change. Danish SU changes on 1 January 2027 for this cohort.
intervals.consequenceIfWrong: A student plans a budget around money they will not receive.

rollover.note: The annual rollover moves the site from one IB session and university intake to the next. It is a checklist, not a script, because most steps need a person to read a page and decide.
steps: Bump targetIntake on every Destination and create the new intake's Opportunities. Opportunity ids carry the intake, so the previous cycle's records stay intact and comparable.
Re-verify every Application Milestone. Any date carried over from the previous cycle must be marked provisional: true until the authority republishes it.
Re-verify every entry requirement against the programme's own page for the new admission year.
Re-fetch the grade conversion table. Denmark publishes the new one by 1 March.
Re-check tuition for the new academic year, and remove any figure whose year cannot be established.
Confirm each English-taught programme is still running and still in English.
Run scripts/freshness.mjs --rollover to list every date-bound claim that has not been touched.
Run scripts/watch-sources.mjs to find pages that changed since they were last read.
Archive the previous cycle's dist/data.json so a student who acted on it can see what they saw.
